extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, and attorneys/agents registered to practice before the USPTO (also patent examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on requesting 'special' status (accelerated processing), suspension/deferral of action, and related procedural requirements for U.S. patent applications (including energy, biotech, recombinant DNA, superconductivity, HIV/AIDS/cancer, counter-terrorism, accelerated examination, suspension, and deferral).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for energy-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought because the invention materially contributes to (A) the discovery or development of energy resources, or (B) the more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: category (A) developments in fossil fuels, hydrogen fuel technologies, nuclear, solar; category (B) inventions reducing energy consumption in combustion systems, industrial equipment, household appliances. No fee required (37 CFR 1.102(c)). If disclosure is not clear that the claimed invention materially contributes to category (A) or (B), the petition must be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 by the applicant, assignee, or registered attorney/agent explaining how the materiality standard is met. The materiality standard does not permit speculation about how a hypothetical end-user might specially apply the invention to materially enhance the environment, nor permit claiming benefit merely because a minor aspect may enhance the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions relating to recombinant DNA research safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications relating to safety of research in the field of recombinant DNA upon appropriate petition and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 by the applicant, assignee, or registered attorney/agent explaining the relationship of the invention to safety of recombinant DNA research. The 37 CFR 1.17(h) fee must be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites for accelerated examination (special status for new applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted special status (accelerated examination) provided applicant complies with each of the following items: (A) submits a petition to make special accompanied by the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(h); (B) presents all claims directed to a single invention or will make an election without traverse; (C) submits a statement that a pre-examination search was made, listing field of search by class/subclass and other sources; (D) submits one copy each of the references deemed most closely related; and (E) submits a detailed discussion of the references pointing out, with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office determines claims are not obviously directed to a single invention and no election without traverse is made, the petition will be denied and application awaits regular turn. A foreign patent office search satisfies (C) if corresponding foreign claims are of same/similar scope. References in (D) are required only if not already of record. The discussion in (E) must meet the particularity of 37 CFR 1.111(b),(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election to a single invention requirement for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must present all claims directed to a single invention, or if Office determines claims are not directed to a single invention, applicant must make an election without traverse as prerequisite to grant of special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election may be made at time of filing petition. If applicant fails to include election and Office determines requirement should be made, telephone restriction practice will be followed. If applicant refuses to make an election without traverse, application will not be further examined at that time and petition denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination search statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a statement(s) that a pre-examination search was made, listing the field of search by class and subclass, publication, Chemical Abstracts, foreign patents, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pre-examination search must be directed to the invention as claimed in the application for which special status is requested. A search made by a foreign patent office satisfies this requirement if the claims in the corresponding foreign application are of the same or similar scope to the U.S. claims for which special status is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of closest references for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit one copy each of the references deemed most closely related to the subject matter encompassed by the claims if said references are not already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists the examiner's restricted search and speeds prosecution; only copies not already in the file must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed discussion of references (37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c) particularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a detailed discussion of the references which points out, with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion must be specific and address how each reference does or does not teach or render obvious the claimed subject matter—meeting the same particularity as required for replies under 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of defective accelerated-exam requests and opportunity to perfect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for special status does not meet all prerequisites, applicant will be notified of defects and given one opportunity to perfect the request in a renewed petition to make special.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If perfected on the first renewed petition, request will be granted. If not perfected in the first renewed petition, any additional renewed petitions may or may not be considered at the discretion of the Technology Center Special Program Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal from granted special (accelerated) status
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a request has been granted, prosecution will proceed according to the accelerated procedure; there is no provision for 'withdrawal' from this special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that acceptance of special status commits the application to the accelerated prosecution flow described in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination first action, search scope, and shortened reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will take up the application before other categories (except those clearly in condition for allowance and those with set time limits) and will give a complete first action including all essential matters as to all claims. The examiner’s search will be restricted to the subject matter encompassed by the claims. A first action rejection will set a 3-month shortened period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The restricted search and requirement for a complete first action speed resolution. Applicants must be prepared to respond within shortened time frames (3 months) or arrange appropriate interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice during accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 3-month period for reply, applicant is encouraged to arrange for an interview with the examiner in order to resolve as many issues as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To afford the examiner time for reflective consideration, applicant or representative should place in the hands of the examiner at least one working day prior to the interview a copy (clearly denoted) of the amendment proposed to be filed in response. That preparatory paper will not become part of the file but will form a basis for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record reply and amendment limits in accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent to the interview, or responsive to the examiner’s first action if no interview was had, applicant will file the 'record' reply; the reply, to be proper, must be restricted to the rejections, objections, and requirements made. Any amendment which would require broadening the search field will be treated as an improper reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid filing amendments that broaden the search field in response to the examiner's first action; such amendments are improper and may disrupt the accelerated procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner final disposition timing in accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will, within 1 month from the date of receipt of applicant’s formal reply, take up the application for final disposition (either a final action terminating with a 3-month period for reply or a notice of allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s reply to any amendment submitted after final rejection should be prompt and may pass the application to issue (form PTOL-303) or provide an examiner’s answer if applicant files an appeal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for superconductivity inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants desiring participation should request that their applications be accorded 'special' status and accompany requests by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include superconductive materials themselves and their manufacture/application. No fee is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer. Applicants should file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) requesting special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should be accompanied by a statement explaining how the invention contributes to the diagnosis, treatment or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer. Fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions materially contributing to countering terrorism
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should petition that their applications be accorded special status; the petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought because the invention materially contributes to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required (see 37 CFR 1.102(c)). If disclosure is not clear that the claimed invention is materially directed to countering terrorism, petition must be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the invention materially contributes. The materiality standard does not permit speculation about hypothetical end-user application nor a benefit merely because some minor aspect may be directed to countering terrorism. Examples of counter-terrorism technologies include detection/identification of explosives, aircraft sensors/security systems, vehicular barricades/disabling systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for biotechnology applications filed by small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-entity applicants may request special status for biotechnology applications by filing a petition with the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) and must: (A) state that small entity status has been established or include a statement establishing small entity status; (B) state that the subject of the patent application is a major asset of the small entity; and (C) state that development will be significantly impaired if examination is delayed, including an explanation of the basis for that statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three statements are required with the petition; supervisory review and fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of a petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special should: (A) be in writing; and (B) identify the application by application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions not meeting these formal requirements may be denied and the application taken up for action in the regular order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and recordation of petitions to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition to make special, regardless of the ground, is made of record in the application file together with the decision thereon. The petition and attached papers will be given a single paper number and so entered in the 'Contents'; the decision will be accorded a separate paper number and similarly entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The part of the Office that rules on the petition is responsible for properly entering that petition and decision in the file. Petitions to make special are decided by the Special Program Examiner of the Technology Center to which the application is assigned. Applications made special will be advanced out of turn and treated as special throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) — petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must: (A) be presented as a separate paper; (B) be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g) (unless cause is the fault of the Office); (C) request a specific and reasonable period of suspension not greater than 6 months; and (D) present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not grant suspension if a reply by applicant to an Office action is outstanding. A petition to suspend to allow submission of an information disclosure statement will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons (37 CFR 1.97 provides adequate recourse). If requirements are not met, the application will be taken up for action in the normal order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(b) and (c) for CPA or RCE — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request suspension under 1.103(b) or (c) for up to 3 months in a continued prosecution application (CPA) or a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114. The request must be filed at the time of filing the CPA or RCE, specify period in whole months (max 3), and include the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i). If filed with an RCE, the RCE must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 (accompanied by submission and fee). If filed with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request specifies no period or exceeds 3 months, Office will assume a 3-month suspension. The processing fee of 1.17(i) is required. An improper RCE/CPA (no filing date, missing submission or fee) means the Office will not recognize the request and will not suspend action; applicant will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing parts or improper CPA/RCE on suspension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filing date is assigned to a design CPA, the request for suspension will be processed even if CPA was not accompanied by CPA basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee; applicant must pay these within 2 months to avoid abandonment. If the CPA or RCE is improper (no filing date or RCE without submission/fee), the Office will not recognize the request for suspension and action will not be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later proper RCE is filed, the request for suspension should be resubmitted. If the request for suspension itself is improper (untimely or without fee 1.17(i)), action will not be suspended and the application will be placed on the examiner’s docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) — requirements and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) must include: (A) a period of suspension in whole months not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date (Office will assume maximum if none specified); (B) the publication fee under 37 CFR 1.18(d); and (C) the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). The Office will not grant deferral unless: (A) the application is an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or resulted from entry of an international application into the national stage after compliance with 37 CFR 1.495; (B) the application was filed on or after November 29, 2000; (C) the applicant has not filed a nonpublication request (or has rescinded it via 37 CFR 1.213(b)); (D) the application is in condition for publication (37 CFR 1.211(c)); and (E) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/37 may be used. A supervisory patent examiner’s approval is required to grant a deferral. If a request is improper, the Office will deny and state reasons (e.g., prior Office action issued, nonpublication not rescinded). Once granted, examination will be deferred until suspension period expires; example timeline provided in MPEP illustrates automatic placement back on examiner’s docket when deferral lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action — effect on patent term adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in patent term adjustment accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reduction equals the number of days beginning on the date a request for suspension of action was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension. See 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1).
